# polaris_principal_credentials (Resource)

Issues new credentials for a Polaris principal. New credentials are issued when the resource is created, and again only when `principal`, `method`, `rotation_triggers` or `client_secret` change. The secret is stored in state as a sensitive value. Destroying the resource only removes it from state: the credentials stay valid. With `RESET`, every previous secret stops working, including `polaris_principal.client_secret`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "polaris_principal" "spark" {
  name = "spark-job"
}

# Issue new credentials every month, and whenever the principal is re-created.
resource "time_rotating" "monthly" {
  rotation_months = 1
}

resource "polaris_principal_credentials" "spark" {
  principal = polaris_principal.spark.name

  rotation_triggers = {
    principal_id = polaris_principal.spark.client_id
    rotated_on   = time_rotating.monthly.id
  }
}

output "spark_client_secret" {
  value     = polaris_principal_credentials.spark.client_secret
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `principal` (String) The name of the principal. Changing this issues new credentials.

### Optional

- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) The new OAuth client secret. Set it to choose the secret yourself (`RESET` only; the server may reject secrets that do not meet its rules), or leave it unset to let Polaris generate one. Changing it issues new credentials.
- `method` (String) How the credentials are issued. `RESET` (default) calls resetCredentials: it needs admin rights on the principal and revokes every previous secret. `ROTATE` calls rotateCredentials: Polaris only allows it for the principal itself, so the provider must authenticate as that principal, and the previous secret keeps working until the next rotation, for zero-downtime rotation. Changing this issues new credentials.
- `rotation_triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that issue new credentials when they change, e.g. a date to rotate on a schedule, or the principal's `client_id` so new credentials follow a re-created principal.

### Read-Only

- `client_id` (String) The OAuth client ID of the principal.
